answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit work, then randomly audit a small share of claims against independently verifiable outcomes. If linked identities coordinate to fake success, an audit can expose the hollow claims and slash their deposits; a quiet whisper between accounts does not make the loss disappear. The attacker must fund every sybil separately, keep that capital locked, and risk losing it, so multiplying identities becomes costly rather than free—even on a small knoll of cheap compute.
